# US-201: return probability per purchase on ASOS, protocols A and B

<!-- Generated by `python -m ml.propensity --raw data/raw --out artifacts` from raw/asos_*.parquet. Do not edit by hand: rerun the command. -->

Every number below comes from ASOS GraphReturns, McGowan et al. 2023, arXiv:2302.14096, OSF c793h, CC BY 4.0; split periods per the paper: train 2021-09-01..2021-10-31, test 2021-10-01..2021-11-30; nature: real; train split 2021-09-01..2021-10-31, test split 2021-10-01..2021-11-30 (the paper's months: events carry no timestamp). Protocols of ADR-10: A = "Paper protocol: features computed over the labelled window, not available at decision time"; B = "Decision-time protocol".

Reproduce from the repository root: `python -m ml.propensity --raw data/raw --out artifacts`. Outputs: `artifacts/models/propensity_A.json`, `artifacts/models/propensity_B.json` (XGBoost JSON), their `_calibrator.json` files, `artifacts/models/propensity_baseline.json` and the metrics with provenance in `artifacts/metrics/us-201-propensity.json`.

## Go/no-go (ADR-10, MOD-01, MOD-06)

Origin: ASOS GraphReturns, McGowan et al. 2023, arXiv:2302.14096, OSF c793h, CC BY 4.0; split periods per the paper: train 2021-09-01..2021-10-31, test 2021-10-01..2021-11-30. Nature: real. Test split, 2021-10-01..2021-11-30. Population: decision-time test events (1,400,482 events). Baseline: returned if customer_loo_return_rate >= 0.3214; missing -> returned.

| Check | Protocol B | Baseline | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 above the baseline | 0.7390 | 0.7208 | pass |
| Cross-entropy below the baseline | 0.5763 | 0.6132 | pass |
| F1 above every single-feature candidate (best test F1 among them) | 0.7390 | 0.7208 | pass |
| Cross-entropy below every candidate (lowest test cross-entropy among them) | 0.5763 | 0.6132 | pass |
| Calibrated: ECE <= 0.05 (MOD-06) | 0.0034 | 0.0019 | pass |

**Protocol B: GO.**

Protocol A (Paper protocol: features computed over the labelled window, not available at decision time), full test set: F1 0.7757 at threshold 0.5 and 0.7859 at the validation threshold, against 0.774 in the paper; the spec threshold F1 >= 0.75 applies to protocol A only: pass. A protocol A number is never product performance (NFR-16).

## Results side by side

Threshold: the calibrated probability above which a purchase is predicted returned, chosen to maximise F1 on the validation split; precision and recall at that threshold. Cross-entropy in nats, ECE over ten equal-width bins, both on calibrated probabilities.

## Features

- **A, XGBoost** (Paper protocol: features computed over the labelled window, not available at decision time), 59 features: `customer_sales`, `customer_returns`, `customer_return_rate`, `customer_reason_share_A`, `customer_reason_share_B`, `customer_reason_share_C`, `customer_reason_share_D`, `customer_reason_share_E`, `customer_reason_share_D2`, `customer_reason_share_F`, `customer_reason_share_G`, `customer_reason_share_H`, `customer_reason_share_I`, `customer_reason_share_J`, `customer_reason_share_K`, `customer_reason_share_L`, `customer_premier`, `variant_sales`, `variant_returns`, `variant_return_rate`, `variant_reason_share_A`, `variant_reason_share_B`, `variant_reason_share_C`, `variant_reason_share_D`, `variant_reason_share_E`, `variant_reason_share_D2`, `variant_reason_share_F`, `variant_reason_share_G`, `variant_reason_share_H`, `variant_reason_share_I`, `variant_reason_share_J`, `variant_reason_share_K`, `variant_reason_share_L`, `avg_price_gbp`, `avg_discount`, `product_type_jeans`, `product_type_producttype_a`, `product_type_producttype_b`, `product_type_producttype_c`, `product_type_producttype_d`, `product_type_producttype_e`, `product_type_producttype_f`, `product_type_producttype_g`, `product_type_producttype_h`, `product_type_producttype_i`, `product_type_producttype_j`, `brand_brand_a`, `brand_brand_b`, `brand_brand_c`, `brand_brand_d`, `brand_brand_e`, `brand_brand_f`, `brand_brand_g`, `brand_brand_i`, `brand_brand_j`, `brand_brand_k`, `brand_pull_bear`, `has_customer_features`, `has_variant_features`.
  Largest shares of total gain (contribution to the score, not a cause): `customer_return_rate` 0.85, `variant_return_rate` 0.10, `variant_reason_share_K` 0.01, `avg_price_gbp` 0.01, `variant_sales` 0.00.
- **B, XGBoost** (Decision-time protocol), 30 features: `customer_sales_loo`, `customer_returns_loo`, `variant_sales_loo`, `variant_returns_loo`, `avg_price_gbp`, `avg_discount`, `product_type_jeans`, `product_type_producttype_a`, `product_type_producttype_b`, `product_type_producttype_c`, `product_type_producttype_d`, `product_type_producttype_e`, `product_type_producttype_f`, `product_type_producttype_g`, `product_type_producttype_h`, `product_type_producttype_i`, `product_type_producttype_j`, `brand_brand_a`, `brand_brand_b`, `brand_brand_c`, `brand_brand_d`, `brand_brand_e`, `brand_brand_f`, `brand_brand_g`, `brand_brand_i`, `brand_brand_j`, `brand_brand_k`, `brand_pull_bear`, `has_customer_features`, `has_variant_features`.
  Largest shares of total gain (contribution to the score, not a cause): `customer_returns_loo` 0.43, `customer_sales_loo` 0.30, `variant_returns_loo` 0.08, `variant_sales_loo` 0.06, `avg_price_gbp` 0.06.
- No model holds a forbidden feature (rule 6, FAIR-01: gender, country, age, names, hashes and raw identifiers, checked by `contracts.parquet.is_forbidden_feature` before training); protocol B holds no rate, reason share or node aggregate.

## Method and limitations

- XGBoost with the paper's hyperparameters (objective binary:logistic, eval_metric logloss, tree_method hist, max_depth 4, eta 0.1, gamma 1.0, min_child_weight 1.0, lambda 2.0), early stopping after 5 rounds on the validation log loss, at most 2000 rounds (our cap), seed 42.
- Same splits for every model: the ASOS train and test splits, and seeded random 10% of the train split: early stopping, isotonic calibration, F1 thresholds and the baseline rule.
- Left joins by split with explicit nulls: an event without a customer or variant row keeps NaN features and has_customer_features / has_variant_features = 0. Product attributes come from the variant table of the event's own split.
- Protocol B uses leave-one-out counts: the customer's and the variant's sales and returns minus the event itself. Every customer and variant row of the dataset has at least one return, so a row whose only return is the event exists because the event was returned: its leave-one-out returns are 0, and every such event whose row's counts hold it is returned (table above; the few exceptions are rows whose counts were clipped). These events are left out of the decision-time population, where protocol B is trained, calibrated and judged; this refines ADR-10, which did not foresee it. Left in training, they teach the model that a customer or variant with no other return returns this purchase, the opposite of what a store sees at decision time, and they inflate the full-test-set numbers. The diagnostic row 'B trained on every event' shows the same features trained with them; it is never saved or used.
- Protocol B still sees other purchases of the same window: ASOS events carry no timestamp (ADR-10). The variant aggregates are identical in the train and test tables, so they also count test-period purchases.
- The dataset holds only customers with at least one return (paper): its rates do not describe all ASOS customers, and the model meets customers without returns only in the synthetic store (distribution shift, risk R-07).
- Protocol A aggregates are computed over the labelled window: its numbers measure the dataset, not the product, and serve benchmarks B1, B2 and the comparison with the paper.
